import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time columns to datetime for better handling
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Set the datetime column as the index
coffee_sales.set_index('datetime', inplace=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and hour
hourly_sales = coffee_sales.groupby([coffee_sales.index.hour, 'product'])['total'].sum().unstack()

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.lineplot(data=hourly_sales, palette='tab10', linewidth=2.5)

# Adding labels and title
plt.title('Hourly Sales by Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(range(0, 24))
plt.legend(title='Product', title_fontsize='13', loc='upper right')

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time columns to datetime for better handling
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Set the datetime column as the index
coffee_sales.set_index('datetime', inplace=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and hour
hourly_sales = coffee_sales.groupby([coffee_sales.index.hour, 'product'])['total'].sum().unstack()

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.lineplot(data=hourly_sales, palette='tab10', linewidth=2.5)

# Adding labels and title
plt.title('Hourly Sales by Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(range(0, 24))
